01.r: Moses is to give the Levites a further word.
01.n: A perfect with 'and', which carries on the instruction of the verses before. The KJV and most others make the 'and' a 'therefore'; YLT renders the perfect form literally, 'thou hast said'.

03.r: Once the Levites have lifted their contribution off the tithe.
03.n: Literally 'in your lifting up': an infinitive with 'in' and 'your', which Hebrew uses for 'when you'. It is the causative form of a verb that Gesenius and BDB give as to rise, be high, the same verb as in the verse before. YLT keeps the Hebrew shape.

04.r: Marks 'its best' as the object of 'lift up'.
04.n: This small word marks a definite direct object and has no English equivalent; it is counted here with 'its best'.

05.r: The finest part of the tithe, the portion owed to the LORD.
05.n: Literally 'its fat'. Gesenius gives fat, and figuratively the best or most excellent of any kind. Geneva and YLT keep 'fat'.
t: all the goodly and the better things

06.r: From the tithe the Levites received.

07.r: What remains is to be treated as the Levites' own harvest.
07.n: A passive form of a verb whose primary idea, Gesenius suggests, is computing or reckoning. A perfect with 'and' after the 'when' clause, so 'then it shall be'. The 'it' is most naturally the tithe left after the best is lifted out; that is a reading of the context, not something the verse names.

08.r: The Levites are the ones for whom it counts.
08.n: The DRC and BSB say 'to you', since the Levites are being addressed.

09.r: Compares the Levites' remaining share to a farmer's harvest.
09.n: Gesenius gives produce, as of the earth, and cites this verse for the produce of the threshing floor and of the winepress. The KJV's 'increase' renders a different Hebrew word from the one our register calls 'increase', so we say 'produce' here.
t: as if you had given the firstfruits

10.r: The floor where grain was threshed: the grain harvest.
10.n: Gesenius: a level place, made smooth, especially a floor on which grain is trodden out. The noun has no article: 'a threshing floor'.

11.r: The same comparison, for the wine harvest.

12.r: Where grapes were pressed: the wine harvest.
12.n: Gesenius gives first the vat of the winepress, the cistern into which the juice flows from the press, and second the winepress itself; BDB gives wine vat. YLT says 'wine-vat'.

03.n: ὅταν ἀφαιρῆτε, 'when you take off', the same verb the Greek uses for 'lift up' in the verse before.

05.n: ἀπαρχή, 'firstfruits, first portion', where the Hebrew says 'its fat', its best.

07.n: Our Greek text splits one word in two: λογὶς θήσεται is λογισθήσεται, 'it shall be reckoned', from λογίζομαι.

08.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched form is marked loose. Our Greek text spells the word Λευείταις.

10.n: The Greek says 'from a threshing floor' where the Hebrew has 'of'.

11.n: The first word, printed κα in our Greek text, is καὶ cut short.
